### 🚀 Quick Plan for Your Dog‑Walking Website **What we’re building**: A one‑page site that shows your name, a short “About” blurb, a “Services & Prices” section, your contact details, and maybe a photo of your pup. **Who uses it**: You (or anyone searching for dog‑walking services). **Risk level**: **Green** – no logins, no personal data, no payments. **Key features**: 1. **Header** with your business name and a catchy tagline. 2. **About** – a paragraph (or two) about you and your love for dogs. 3. **Services & Prices** – a simple list of walk options and rates. 4. **Photo** – an image of you or your dog (optional). 5. **Contact** – phone number, email address, and a simple “Get a quote” button that opens the user’s mail app. **Where to host**: Free sites like Netlify Drop, GitHub Pages, or Vercel (all give you an HTTPS URL). **What you need to do**: - Pick a name and tagline. - Write the short “About” text. - List the walks you offer and their prices. - Provide a photo URL or a local image. - Give your contact phone and email. --- #### Step‑by‑step (in plain language) 1. **Create a folder** on your computer called `dog-walking-website`. 2. **Make a file** inside it called `index.html`. 3. **Copy‑paste the code below** into that file. 4. **Open the file** in a web browser – you’ll see the site as it will look online. ```html YOUR BUSINESS NAME – Dog Walking Services

YOUR BUSINESS NAME

A trusted dog‑walking service for your furry friends.

About Me

YOUR-SHORT-ABOUT-TEXT-HERE. I love dogs and give them safe, energetic strolls that keep them happy and healthy.

Services & Prices

  • 30‑minute walk – $15
  • 60‑minute walk – $25
  • Group walk (up to 3 dogs) – $30

Contact

Phone: +1‑234‑567‑890

Email: youremail@example.com

``` > **Replace the placeholder text** (e.g., `YOUR BUSINESS NAME`, `YOUR-IMAGE-URL.jpg`, `YOUR-SHORT-ABOUT-TEXT-HERE`, `+1234567890`, `youremail@example.com`) with your real details. 5. **Save the file**. 6. **Test locally**: double‑click `index.html` to view it. 7. **Publish**: - **GitHub Pages**: Put the folder in a new GitHub repo, enable GitHub Pages in Settings → Pages → Source → main → `/`. - **Netlify Drop**: Drag the folder onto the Netlify Drop site (https://app.netlify.com/drop) and it will give you a URL. - **Vercel**: `git init`, push to a new repo, and connect to Vercel for automatic deployment. You’ll now have a live, HTTPS‑protected website that showcases your dog‑walking business with no risk of data leaks or hidden costs. 🎉 Let me know if you’d like a quick walkthrough of any step or want to add a tiny photo carousel or a Google‑Maps address before going live.
